guarantees.claim: On active-low reset (rst_ni=0), app_id is synchronously cleared to 0.
When clr_appid is high (and no reset), app_id is cleared to 0, overriding any set_appid.
When set_appid is high and clr_appid is low (no reset), app_id is updated with app_id_d.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i and set_appid and !clr_appid and !rst_ni

guarantees.claim: When neither clr_appid nor set_appid is asserted, app_id retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: app_id_d must provide a valid, non-X value when set_appid is sampled high.
assumptions.risk: app_id could capture X or an invalid index, causing mis-selection or undefined behavior in downstream logic.

uncertain_points.claim: The intended semantics of app_id value 0 (comment 'Do not select any') is not defined in this chunk; it is unclear if 0 is a safe default or an invalid index.
uncertain_points.risk: If 0 is a valid application index, reset or clr_appid may unintentionally select an active context, causing security or functional issues.

uncertain_points.claim: The app_id register is used outside this chunk; its effect on application isolation, data steering, or access control must be verified in the integrating logic.
uncertain_points.risk: Improper enforcement of app_id could lead to cross-application data leakage or unauthorized operations.

uncertain_points.claim: The hardcoded priority of clr_appid over set_appid (when both asserted simultaneously) is not documented; it may mask a protocol error.
uncertain_points.risk: If both are accidentally asserted, an intended set operation is suppressed and app_id is cleared, potentially causing a loss of configuration.
